title: Stow an unplugged hair dryer barrel-down in a tapered bathroom wall holster
instruction: Stow the unplugged hair dryer in the wall holder so it remains supported.
context: Putting the hair dryer back in its bathroom wall holder is an everyday chore, and coil holders like this are common in hotel, gym and home bathrooms: a steel spiral that narrows from 90 mm at the top to 60 mm. The dryer lies on its side and is held by its handle, as a person does, so the hand has to turn it a quarter turn to barrel-down, carry it over the coil and lower the barrel through turns that leave about 10 mm per side at the top and 5 mm at the next, then let go. It must stay in the coil with no hand on it. The hand cannot follow the barrel inside, so the turn and the lowering have to be right before release.
setup: A fixed 298 x 298 x 9 mm white porcelain wall tile stands on the table, front face at x=0.4055 m, centred at y=-0.125 m. A fixed stainless-steel Smedbo HK323 style hair dryer holder (155 mm high x 129 mm long x 100 mm deep, 302 g) is mounted to it with its axis at x=0.325, y=-0.125 m: a 90 x 155 x 10.6 mm steel mounting plate on the tile, two 12 x 5 mm arms, and four rigid 4 mm wire rings 257, 207, 156 and 106 mm above the table with clear openings of 90, 80, 70 and 60 mm. An unplugged Panasonic EH-NA2C style hair dryer (one rigid plastic-like body, 154 x 140 x 79 mm, 368 g without nozzle, uniform density) lies on its side at x=0.190, y=-0.220 m, barrel toward the holder (+x), handle toward the right arm (-y); it settles rolled 13 deg onto the handle tip. Its barrel is a 70 mm nominal cylinder 105 mm long, behind it a 79 mm rear housing 49 mm long; the handle is 25 mm wide, 35 mm thick and projects 61 mm from the housing. The cord is omitted.
scoring: 0.0 if the dryer falls more than 10 mm below the tabletop, leaves the 700 x 900 mm tabletop, or the holder moves more than 10 mm; these faults persist for the rest of the trial. Otherwise 1.0 if the dryer is barrel-down (axis within 32 deg of vertical), its barrel tip is at least 20 mm below the top ring (and no lower than 15 mm under the lowest ring), its barrel centre is within 12 mm of the holder axis and it touches the coil (contact read from the holder's collision shapes), and in addition the dryer is still (<= 12 mm/s, <= 0.15 rad/s), both hands are open to at least 76 mm, no robot link presses on the dryer with more than 0.05 N, and the coil bears at least 0.05 N, all held without a break for 1.0 s. Otherwise 0.5 if only the first set holds (barrel-down, centred, in at least 20 mm and touching the coil), for example while the dryer is still held. All other outcomes score 0.0. On a real holder: ruler for depth and centring, a gauge or scale for the 0.05 N, video for the second.
fidelity: One rigid dryer (convex barrel, rear housing, handle), uniform density, nominal 70 mm barrel, cord and nozzle omitted. The holder is four separate rigid 4 mm rings (90/80/70/60 mm), not a continuous spring spiral. The dryer ends wedged barrel-down in the 70 mm ring, held by the rings and gravity, not hanging from its handle. Default friction (1.2). The scripted demo is tuned to the measured rest pose and carry sag; one passing run, robustness not checked.
reset_notes: Return the dryer to its marked lying pose, with the barrel toward the holster and the cord routed out of the workspace; inspect the holder and tile for movement or damage.
